{"review_id":"r1-correctness","slice":"WP-SCP-024/024B-core","lens":"correctness","reviewer":"sonnet-r1-correctness","date":"2026-05-09","verdict":"CHANGES_REQUESTED","summary":"The 024B-core slice delivers a coherent scaffolder, adopter-wrapper template, and cascade-status enforcement CLI. Argument validation, sed substitution with marker-completeness guard, MANIFEST SHA256 audit, and the five-path state machine are all structurally sound. The template mirrors the canonical wrapper shape, Renovate marker placement is correct, and least-privilege permissions (contents:read + statuses:write only) are enforced. D-044, the STATUS.md chain entry, and the plan-doc §6 amendment are correctly scoped and filed. However, a critical logic defect exists in check-invocation-log-entry.sh: the two-pass cascade-status parse uses two inconsistent regex anchors. The dispatch_note_mode first-pass regex (^[ \\t]*cascade-status:) allows leading whitespace, while the cascade_status second-pass regex (^cascade-status:) requires strict line-start. Because dispatch_note_mode runs first and exits 0 on 'not applicable', injecting a single indented '  cascade-status: not applicable' line before any real cascade-status declaration bypasses all enforcement. This directly violates the plan-doc fail-closed contract. Three downstream issues compound this: the case statement's 'not applicable' branch is unreachable dead code (cascade_status regex [a-z-]+ excludes spaces, so 'not applicable' can never be returned); no test covers the bypass scenario; and the run_enable_case helper function (lines 146-195 of the test file) is defined but never called and directly references enable-required-check.sh, a clear extras-carve-out AC violation. One nit: the scaffolder's first denylist case block is a strict subset of the second case block and is dead code.","findings":[{"id":"CORR-CRIT-001","severity":"CRIT","claim":"dispatch_note_mode regex allows leading whitespace (^[ \\t]*cascade-status:), while cascade_status uses strict ^cascade-status:. A DISPATCH-NOTE with '  cascade-status: not applicable' (indented) before 'cascade-status: onboarded' sets dispatch_note_mode='not applicable' → exit 0, skipping the cascade_status check entirely. All enforcement (log-entry check, target-match, TF-row regex, negative log-modification assertion) is bypassed.","evidence":"check-invocation-log-entry.sh:121 — re.search(r'(?m)^[ \\t]*cascade-status:\\s+([^\\r\\n]+?)\\s*$', text). Lines 133-136: if [ \"$dispatch_note_mode\" = \"not applicable\" ]; then exit 0; fi fires before cascade_status is parsed. Line 145 re.findall(r'^cascade-status:...') is never reached in the bypass path. No test exercises the indented-not-applicable-before-onboarded case.","impact":"Fail-closed contract violated. Any real cascade slice DISPATCH-NOTE can be modified with one indented leading line ('  cascade-status: not applicable') to exit 0 without verifying the branch-protection log, target match, TF-row format, or log-not-modified assertion — defeating all four invariant-2 enforcement paths simultaneously.","mitigation":"Remove '[ \\t]*' from the dispatch_note_mode regex at line 121: change r'(?m)^[ \\t]*cascade-status:\\s+([^\\r\\n]+?)\\s*$' to r'(?m)^cascade-status:\\s+([^\\r\\n]+?)\\s*$'. This makes both parsers require strict line-start, closing the bypass while preserving correct behavior for standard non-indented declarations."},{"id":"CORR-MAJ-001","severity":"MAJ","claim":"The case statement branch 'not applicable') at lines 156-160 of check-invocation-log-entry.sh is unreachable dead code. cascade_status uses re.findall(r'^cascade-status:\\s+([a-z-]+)\\s*$', ...) where [a-z-]+ excludes spaces; 'not applicable' contains a space and can never be returned. The branch creates false confidence that 'not applicable' is handled in two places.","evidence":"check-invocation-log-entry.sh:145 — ([a-z-]+) captures only chars in [a-z-]; space is excluded. For 'cascade-status: not applicable', ([a-z-]+) matches 'not' then \\s*$ fails at ' applicable'. findall returns []. Lines 156-160: '\"not applicable\"') branch can never be entered. dispatch_note_mode (line 121) is the sole handler.","impact":"If dispatch_note_mode is ever refactored away (e.g., to unify the two passes), 'cascade-status: not applicable' falls through to FAIL-CLOSED with a misleading error rather than being caught by the supposedly second handler. Dead code also masks the design gap to code reviewers.","mitigation":"Remove the unreachable '\"not applicable\"') case branch (lines 156-160). Alternatively, fix cascade_status regex to also capture 'not applicable' (e.g., replace ([a-z-]+) with ([a-z][a-z -]*)) so the case branch becomes reachable, and document dispatch_note_mode as the primary early-exit handler."},{"id":"CORR-MAJ-002","severity":"MAJ","claim":"run_enable_case function (lines 146-195) is defined but never called in main(), and directly invokes $REPO_ROOT/scripts/enable-required-check.sh at line 157. DISPATCH-NOTE acceptance criteria explicitly requires 'no enable-required-check.sh references in test bodies'. This is residual content from the extras-parking branch.","evidence":"tests/check_invocation_log/test_check_invocation_log_entry.sh:157 — \"$REPO_ROOT/scripts/enable-required-check.sh\" \"$@\". Grep of main() shows run_enable_case is never called. DISPATCH-NOTE §Scope (in): 'Verify NO --restore-mode coupling remains (no run_restore_case helper; no make_restore_fake_gh; no --restore CLI invocations; no enable-required-check.sh references in test bodies).'","impact":"Direct AC violation; extras-carve-out is not clean. The dead function introduces a stale reference to an out-of-scope script, could be accidentally invoked if a future test author copies its call pattern, and signals incomplete cleanup from the extras-parking branch.","mitigation":"Remove the entire run_enable_case function definition (lines 146-195). No callers exist; deletion is safe."},{"id":"CORR-MAJ-003","severity":"MAJ","claim":"No test covers the scenario where '  cascade-status: not applicable' (indented, first) precedes 'cascade-status: onboarded' (non-indented, second) in a DISPATCH-NOTE. Case 14 tests an indented duplicate of the SAME enumerated value; case 15b tests a standard non-indented 'not applicable'. Neither demonstrates or guards against the CORR-CRIT-001 bypass path.","evidence":"test_check_invocation_log_entry.sh case14 DISPATCH-NOTE: '  cascade-status: onboarded\\ncascade-status: onboarded'. case15b DISPATCH-NOTE: 'cascade-status: not applicable\\n...' (non-indented). No case uses '  cascade-status: not applicable\\ncascade-status: onboarded' (indented not-applicable first). CORR-CRIT-001 bypass is therefore undetected by the test suite.","impact":"Test gap masks a full bypass class. CI gives false confidence that the enforcement script correctly rejects indented-not-applicable injection. Without this test, fixing CORR-CRIT-001 cannot be verified as regression-free.","mitigation":"Add a test case: DISPATCH-NOTE = '  cascade-status: not applicable\\ncascade-status: onboarded\\n- **Target:** jrnb2024/pim\\n' with branch-protection-log modified. After CORR-CRIT-001 fix, expected exit is non-zero (dispatch_note_mode does not match 'not applicable'; cascade_status finds exactly one match 'onboarded'; enforcement runs and should pass or fail depending on log state). Before fix, this test would expose the bypass by returning 0."},{"id":"CORR-nit-001","severity":"nit","claim":"The first denylist case block in scaffold-downstream.sh (lines 142-146) checks only /private/var/tmp|/private/var/tmp/*. The second case block (lines 148-152) already covers /private/var|/private/var/* as a strict superset. The first case fires before the second but matches no path that the second would not also match; it is dead code with an identical error message.","evidence":"scaffold-downstream.sh:142-146 — case \"$OUTPUT_DIR\" in /private/var/tmp|/private/var/tmp/*). scaffold-downstream.sh:149 — /private/var|/private/var/* in the second case matches all paths the first case matches (/private/var/tmp is a member of /private/var/*). Both cases emit the identical die message.","impact":"Dead code; no correctness defect. Clutters the denylist logic and may confuse future editors who see two separate case blocks and assume they are non-overlapping.","mitigation":"Remove the first case block (lines 142-146). The second case already handles /private/var/tmp and all other /private/var/* paths."}]}
